subject: Transition pricing — Sizing, amortized credits, and bridge month options
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Ortiz <j.ortiz@acme-data.ai>, Acme Data Procurement <procurement@acme-data.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transition pricing — Sizing, amortized credits, and bridge month options

Hi Janelle / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — appreciate the openness on expected growth this quarter. Per our conversation, attached is a concise mapping of how we propose to migrate your hosted spend to a dedicated pool with amortized conversion credits and an optional short bridge period to smooth billing during ramp. High level:

Options for baseline GPU pool sizing (examples reflect current Llama-3-70b profile):
- Option A (Conservative): 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs — target 60k inference requests/day (avg payload ~400 tokens).
- Option B (Baseline): 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs — target 130k inference requests/day, recommended for steady-state production.
- Option C (Aggressive): 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs — target 200k+ inference requests/day with headroom for peak batching.

Conversion credit mechanics (proposal):
- We convert existing hosted spend into a dedicated-commit credit at a 0.65x conversion rate (hosted spend $ -> committed monthly $).
- Credits are amortized evenly across the first 12 months of the committed contract by default. Example: $120k hosted credit -> $7,800/month applied to a 12-month amortization.
- Front-loaded option: apply up to 50% of credits in month 1 if Acme needs larger immediate offset (trade-off: shorter amortization).

Bridge month options (to cover overlap ramp risk):
- Standard bridge: 2 months of credits — Month 1: 100% of usual credits applied; Month 2: 50% credits applied.
- Extended bridge: 3 months — Month 1: 100%, Month 2: 75%, Month 3: 50% (available upon request).

Throughput & SLA guarantees:
- Throughput guarantee (aggregate): for Option B (16 GPUs) we target 1,200 requests/min sustained with 99th percentile tail latency < 200 ms for payloads <= 512 tokens on our quantized serving profile.
- Credit for missed SLOs: service credits tiered at 5% monthly credit per each 2% below the 99.5% availability target.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm preferred sizing option (A/B/C).
2) Indicate whether you want default 12-month amortization or front-loaded credits.
3) Tell us if you want Standard or Extended bridge months.

Attached: ACME_Dedicated_Sku_Mapping.xlsx (mapping of hosted SKUs to dedicated commits) and Redwood_Transition_Pricing_v3.pdf (rate card + examples).

If convenient, I can set a 30-minute call early next week to finalize numbers for procurement.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189

Subject: Re: Transition pricing — Sizing, amortized credits, and bridge month options

Hi Olga,

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we bring procurement into the contract review: 

1) How does the 0.65x conversion rate handle existing committed discounts applied to our hosted usage? We had a promotional discount applied over the last 6 months.
2) If we choose the front-loaded option (50% in month 1), can you confirm whether that reduces the total credit pool or simply accelerates application?
3) For the throughput guarantee, can you provide an example SLA calculation tied to our current monthly host request profile (we hit ~95k requests/month now but hit spikes up to 20% higher during marketing pushes).

Procurement note: procurement@acme-data.ai will need a spreadsheet with a per-month amortization schedule and knockout language for the bridge month mechanics.

We'd like to schedule a call next Wednesday (Oct 13) at 10am PT if that works.

Best,
Janelle Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Data
j.ortiz@acme-data.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: sample amortization and conversion examples for Acme

Folks — drafting the detailed examples to send back, notes below (will attach a clean worksheet when done):

- Promo handled: discounts historically applied on hosted spend are netted before conversion. So the 0.65x conversion multiplies the net hosted invoice (post-discount). Example: if Acme had $100k hosted bill and it included a $10k promo discount, we convert $90k -> $58,500 credit at 0.65x.

- Front-load mechanics: front-loading accelerates application but does not change total credit pool. It simply applies a higher portion earlier, reducing the remaining monthly amortized line items. Example (using $60k credit, 12-month amortization): default: $5k/month; front-load 50%: month1 $30k applied, then remaining $30k amortized over next 11 months (~$2.73k/month).

- Bridge month cost modeling: assume conservative ramp where dedicated run-rate reaches 80% of provisioned capacity by end of month 2. With the standard bridge (100% then 50%), net cash impact for Acme vs hosted for first 2 months is roughly neutral for many profiles. The attached worksheet will show a line-by-line.

- SLA language: propose our standard template with a money-back credit schedule (we'll provide exact contract language for procurement).

I recommend we propose Option B (16 GPUs) as the baseline and include an aggressive ramp clause to add 8 GPUs if 30-day rolling avg usage exceeds 85% for >14 days. Marcus: can you confirm GPU SKU availability for Nov start?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Ortiz <j.ortiz@acme-data.ai>, Acme Data Procurement <procurement@acme-data.ai>

Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transition pricing — Sizing, amortized credits, and bridge month options

Hi Janelle — following up with the specifics Karthik outlined and a refined offer we can stand behind: 

Final offer (summary):
- Baseline: Option B (16 A100-eq GPUs). Committed monthly $: $85,000/mo.
- Conversion credit: 0.65x applied to net hosted spend, amortized over 12 months by default. For Acme example hosted spend of $120k net -> $78k credit -> $6,500/month applied.
- Bridge: Standard two-month bridge as proposed (M1 100% credit application; M2 50%). If Acme prefers a 3-month ramp, we can provide Extended bridge (M1 100%, M2 75%, M3 50%) but require a 24-month commit instead of 12 to balance economics.
- SLA/throughput: Guarantee 1,200 requests/min (sustained) for the 16 GPU pool with 99th pct latency <200ms for <=512 tokens. If we fail SLO more than twice in a calendar quarter, we trigger a remediation plan + a service credit of up to 10% of monthly committed fee depending on severity.

Procurement: attached is a per-month amortization schedule exported to the workbook (see "amort_schedule" sheet) and the redlined clause language we recommend for the conversion-credit and bridge mechanics.

If that looks good I can pull legal-internal to draft an MSA addendum and route via DocuSign. Would you like us to model the alternative (front-load 50% month1) in the same amortization sheet?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Olga and team — this is clear and actionable. Procurement (cc'd) will review the spreadsheet; a couple of points from our side: 

- We'd prefer the Extended bridge (3 months) but ask that you keep a 12-month commit if possible. If you can front-load more credits into month 1 (e.g., 70%) we will accept the 12-month term — can you confirm if that is allowable?
- Please include explicit clause: if traffic drops >30% sustained for >60 days (post-transition) dedicated commit can be scaled down with a 30-day notice without penalty (we'll accept a negotiated minimum committed floor).

Assuming those two items are clarified, we are prepared to move to an MSA addendum and scheduling the sign-off call — Wednesday Oct 13 at 10am PT works for us.

-Janelle
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Data
